evals.prompt: Generate a multi-source Application called 'webapp' in the argocd namespace that combines a Helm chart from oci://registry.example.com/charts/webapp at version 2.x with environment-specific values from a Git repo https://github.com/org/config.git (branch main, path envs/production/values.yaml). Deploy to namespace 'webapp-prod' on in-cluster. Use automated sync with selfHeal but WITHOUT prune (the team wants manual prune control). Use valuesObject (not the deprecated string values field) for any inline Helm values. Set server-side apply and respect ignore differences for /spec/replicas on Deployments.
evals.expected_output: A multi-source Application using spec.sources[] array (not spec.source singular), with one Helm source and one Git source providing values via $values ref, automated sync without prune, ServerSideApply, and ignoreDifferences.
expectations: Output uses spec.sources (plural array) not spec.source (singular) — multi-source Applications require the array form
Output contains exactly two entries in the sources array

First source is the Helm/OCI chart: repoURL is the registry host and path WITHOUT the oci:// scheme (registry.example.com/charts) and chart: webapp is a separate field — per Argo CD docs, "the oci:// syntax is not included" in repoURL
Helm source uses targetRevision with semver constraint 2.x or similar
Second source is Git with repoURL: https://github.com/org/config.git
Git source has ref.targetRevision: main and path containing envs/production
Helm source references the Git source values via $values syntax (e.g., $values/envs/production/values.yaml)
Output does NOT use helm.values as a string — uses helm.valuesObject or the $values ref pattern
Sync policy has automated with selfHeal: true but prune: false or prune omitted
syncOptions includes ServerSideApply=true
ignoreDifferences entry for group apps kind Deployment with jsonPointers /spec/replicas
Destination namespace is webapp-prod with server https://kubernetes.default.svc

evals.prompt: Create an ApplicationSet using the merge generator that combines a cluster generator (selecting clusters labeled tier=production) with a git file generator reading config from https://github.com/org/fleet-config.git at path 'clusters/{{name}}/config.json'. The merge key should be 'name' so cluster-specific config from Git overrides the cluster generator defaults. Use goTemplate with goTemplateOptions missingkey=error. Each generated Application should deploy from an OCI Helm chart oci://ghcr.io/org/app at the version specified in the config file's 'appVersion' field. Enable preserveResourcesOnDeletion so the generated Applications' cluster resources survive deletion of the ApplicationSet. Add an ignoreApplicationDifferences entry to ignore changes to spec.source.targetRevision so the image updater can modify it without causing drift.
evals.expected_output: An ApplicationSet with merge generator combining cluster and git file generators, goTemplateOptions, OCI Helm source, preserveResourcesOnDeletion at spec level, and ignoreApplicationDifferences.
expectations: Output contains kind: ApplicationSet with apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
Output has goTemplate: true AND goTemplateOptions containing missingkey=error
Output uses a merge generator with mergeKeys containing 'name'
Merge generator contains a clusters generator with selector matchLabels tier: production
Merge generator contains a git file generator with repoURL https://github.com/org/fleet-config.git
Git file generator path references clusters/{{.name}}/config.json or equivalent Go template syntax

Template source points at the OCI registry host and path WITHOUT the oci:// scheme (e.g. repoURL: ghcr.io/org with the chart name in a separate chart: field) — consistent with eval 1 and the Argo CD docs' "the oci:// syntax is not included"
Template source targetRevision references the appVersion field from the config (e.g., {{.appVersion}})
preserveResourcesOnDeletion: true is under spec.syncPolicy (NOT at spec level and NOT under strategy) — spec.preserveResourcesOnDeletion is not in the CRD and is silently pruned by the API server
ignoreApplicationDifferences is present with jsonPointers or jqPathExpressions targeting spec.source.targetRevision

evals.prompt: Generate an Argo Rollout for 'checkout-svc' in namespace 'checkout' with blue-green strategy. Active service is 'checkout-active', preview service is 'checkout-preview'. Do NOT auto-promote — require manual approval. Add a prePromotionAnalysis that runs an AnalysisTemplate called 'smoke-test' which uses a Kubernetes Job provider (not Prometheus). The Job should run an image 'registry.example.com/smoke-tests:latest' that curls the preview service and exits 0 on success. The analysis should have a single measurement with no interval (run once). Also configure scaleDownDelaySeconds to 600 so the old ReplicaSet stays around for 10 minutes after promotion. Generate both the Rollout and the AnalysisTemplate.
evals.expected_output: A Rollout with blue-green strategy, manual promotion, prePromotionAnalysis referencing a Job-based AnalysisTemplate, and scaleDownDelaySeconds.
expectations: Output contains kind: Rollout with strategy.blueGreen (not canary)
Blue-green config has activeService: checkout-active and previewService: checkout-preview
autoPromotionEnabled is explicitly set to false
prePromotionAnalysis references templates with templateName: smoke-test
scaleDownDelaySeconds is set to 600
Output contains a separate AnalysisTemplate kind with name: smoke-test
AnalysisTemplate metric uses provider.job (not prometheus, not web)
Job spec container image is registry.example.com/smoke-tests:latest
Job container command or args references the preview service URL or hostname
AnalysisTemplate metric has count: 1 or count omitted (single measurement, no interval)

evals.prompt: Set up Argo CD notifications with TWO notification services: 1) Slack for the 'platform-alerts' channel on sync failures with a template using Slack Block Kit (not legacy attachments) — use a section block with mrkdwn text showing app name, sync status, and error message, plus an actions block with a button linking to the ArgoCD UI. 2) GitHub commit status updates on the 'infra' repo https://github.com/org/infra using a GitHub App (appID and installationID from secret, not a PAT). The GitHub trigger should fire on every sync operation and set the commit status to success/failure/pending based on the operation phase. Use oncePer: app.status.operationState.syncResult.revision to avoid duplicate statuses for the same commit. Show all ConfigMap entries, Secret entries, and the Application annotations needed.
evals.expected_output: Complete notification setup with Slack Block Kit template, GitHub App commit status, oncePer dedup, and proper annotations.
expectations: ConfigMap contains service.slack config referencing $slack-token
ConfigMap contains service.github config with appID and installationID referencing secret keys
Secret contains slack-token key
Secret contains github-app-privateKey or similar key for GitHub App authentication
Slack template uses blocks array with section type and mrkdwn (not legacy attachments format)
Slack template includes an actions block with a button element linking to argocdUrl
GitHub trigger uses oncePer referencing app.status.operationState.syncResult.revision
GitHub trigger condition maps operation phases to commit status states (success/failure/pending)
Application annotation for Slack: notifications.argoproj.io/subscribe.on-sync-failed.slack
Application annotation for GitHub: notifications.argoproj.io/subscribe referencing the github trigger and service

evals.prompt: I'm deploying Argo CD on OpenShift using the OpenShift GitOps Operator. Generate: 1) An ArgoCD custom resource (the operator CRD, not raw Argo CD manifests) in the openshift-gitops namespace with HA disabled, Route enabled with reencrypt TLS, OpenShift OAuth via Dex, RBAC that maps 'cluster-admins' group to admin role with default readonly policy, resource exclusions for Tekton TaskRun/PipelineRun and OLM InstallPlan, and notifications enabled. 2) A namespace-scoped ArgoCD instance for the 'platform-team' namespace with a Route and sourceNamespaces set. 3) Show the label needed on a target namespace 'platform-staging' so the namespace-scoped instance can manage it. 4) Explain what happens differently on OpenShift vs vanilla Kubernetes regarding SCCs when running Argo Rollouts pods.
evals.expected_output: ArgoCD CRD (argoproj.io/v1beta1) with OpenShift-specific configuration, namespace-scoped instance, managed-by label, and SCC explanation.
expectations: Uses apiVersion argoproj.io/v1beta1 kind ArgoCD (not v1alpha1, not raw Deployment manifests)
Cluster-scoped instance in openshift-gitops namespace (not argocd)
spec.server.route.enabled true with tls.termination reencrypt
spec.sso.provider: dex with spec.sso.dex.openShiftOAuth: true — NOT top-level spec.dex, which is no longer supported from Argo CD Operator v0.8.0 onwards and silently fails to configure SSO
RBAC policy maps cluster-admins to role:admin
RBAC defaultPolicy is role:readonly
resourceExclusions includes tekton.dev TaskRun and PipelineRun
resourceExclusions includes operators.coreos.com InstallPlan
spec.notifications.enabled true
Namespace-scoped instance in platform-team namespace with route and sourceNamespaces
Target namespace label argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by pointing to the instance namespace
Explains that OpenShift uses SecurityContextConstraints (SCCs) instead of PodSecurityPolicies and Rollout pods need appropriate SCC bindings

evals.prompt: I need to set up Argo CD for a multi-tenant platform where 3 teams (frontend, backend, data) each manage their own Applications in their own namespaces. I want a single Argo CD instance, not separate instances per team. Each team should only be able to deploy to their own namespaces and access their own Git repos. The frontend team uses namespace 'team-frontend-apps', the backend team uses 'team-backend-apps', and the data team uses 'team-data-apps'. Generate: 1) The argocd-cmd-params-cm ConfigMap change to enable this, 2) An AppProject for the frontend team that restricts them to their namespace, repos matching 'https://github.com/org/frontend-*', and only allows Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, and Ingresses (no cluster-scoped resources), 3) A sample Application in the team-frontend-apps namespace referencing the project, 4) Show the RBAC policy that allows the 'frontend-devs' SSO group to get/sync apps in their project and namespace only.
evals.expected_output: ConfigMap with application.namespaces, AppProject with sourceNamespaces restricting to team namespace, Application in non-argocd namespace, and RBAC with three-part <project>/<namespace>/<app> syntax.
expectations: ConfigMap argocd-cmd-params-cm with data.application.namespaces listing team namespaces
AppProject has spec.sourceNamespaces containing team-frontend-apps
AppProject has sourceRepos restricted to https://github.com/org/frontend-*
AppProject has destinations restricted to frontend team namespaces only
AppProject has clusterResourceWhitelist that is empty or absent (no cluster-scoped resources)
AppProject has namespaceResourceWhitelist listing only Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, Ingress
Sample Application metadata.namespace is team-frontend-apps (NOT argocd)
Application spec.project references the frontend team project
RBAC policy uses three-part syntax: project/namespace/app (not legacy two-part)
RBAC policy scopes frontend-devs to only their project and namespace
Does NOT suggest running multiple Argo CD instances — uses single instance pattern
Mentions switching resource tracking to annotation or annotation+label for long composite names

evals.prompt: We have 200 edge clusters behind restrictive firewalls where the control plane cannot reach the cluster API servers. We need GitOps on every cluster with centralized observability. Each edge cluster should be fully autonomous — if it loses connectivity to the control plane, it must continue reconciling. When connected, Application status should sync back to the control plane for monitoring. Describe the architecture and components needed. What is the recommended approach? Generate a high-level deployment plan with the components on the control plane cluster vs each edge cluster.
evals.expected_output: Description of argocd-agent with principal on control plane and agent on each workload cluster, autonomous mode, fully autonomous pattern with local Argo CD stack, and the communication model.
expectations: Recommends argocd-agent (not traditional multi-cluster Argo CD)
Describes the principal component running on the control plane
Describes the agent component running on each edge/workload cluster
Specifies autonomous mode (not managed mode) for edge clusters
Recommends the fully autonomous pattern with local Argo CD stack (application-controller + repo-server + redis) on each edge cluster
Explains that agents initiate connections outbound to the principal (not control plane reaching into clusters)
Mentions mTLS or certificate-based authentication between agent and principal
Explains that edge clusters continue reconciling independently during connectivity loss
States that Application status syncs back to control plane for observability when connected
Does NOT suggest storing cluster credentials on the control plane

evals.prompt: I want to set up environment promotion for my app across dev, staging, and production using gitops-promoter. The app repo is on GitHub (org: acme-corp, repo: payments). I want automatic promotion from dev to staging (gated on Argo CD app health), but manual approval for production (gated on both app health and a performance-test check). Also add a security-scan proposed commit status that must pass before merging into any environment. Generate all the resources needed: ScmProvider, GitRepository, PromotionStrategy, and an ArgoCD CommitStatus to report app health. Use a GitHub App for authentication.
evals.expected_output: Complete gitops-promoter setup with ScmProvider (GitHub App), GitRepository, PromotionStrategy with 3 environments and commit status gating, and ArgoCDCommitStatus for health reporting.
expectations: Uses apiVersion promoter.argoproj.io/v1alpha1 for all promoter CRDs
ScmProvider with github field containing appID and installationID
ScmProvider references a Secret for githubAppPrivateKey
GitRepository with github field containing owner: acme-corp and name: payments
GitRepository references the ScmProvider via scmProviderRef
PromotionStrategy with 3 environments: environment/development, environment/staging, environment/production
Production environment has autoMerge: false for manual approval
Dev and staging have autoMerge: true (explicit or default)
activeCommitStatuses includes argocd-health at the strategy level
Production environment has additional activeCommitStatus for performance-test
proposedCommitStatuses includes security-scan at the strategy level
ArgoCDCommitStatus resource (note capitalisation) with the required promotionStrategyRef and applicationSelector — NOT gitRepositoryRef, which is not a field on this kind

evals.name: Notifications on OpenShift GitOps
evals.prompt: Set up Slack notifications for sync failures on our OpenShift GitOps instance in the openshift-gitops namespace. We tried editing argocd-notifications-cm and the changes keep disappearing after a few minutes.
expectations: Identifies the root cause: argocd-notifications-cm is operator-managed on OpenShift GitOps and edits are reconciled away
Sets ArgoCD.spec.notifications.enabled: true to deploy the notifications controller
Uses a NotificationsConfiguration CR (argoproj.io/v1alpha1) instead of editing the ConfigMap
Puts services/templates/triggers as map[string]string keys (service.slack, template.<name>, trigger.<name>), matching the ConfigMap key names
States that the Secret argocd-notifications-secret still has to be created separately — the CR holds no credentials
Does NOT present hand-editing argocd-notifications-cm as the solution

evals.name: Deploy Argo Rollouts on OpenShift GitOps
evals.prompt: How do I get Argo Rollouts running on our OpenShift GitOps cluster? We want it watching every namespace, with the controller pinned to infra nodes.
expectations: Uses a RolloutManager CR (argoproj.io/v1alpha1) rather than installing argo-rollouts manifests directly
Sets namespaceScoped: false for cluster-wide watching
Uses spec.nodePlacement.nodeSelector (and tolerations) for infra node placement
Notes that editing the argo-rollouts Deployment directly is reverted by the operator
Does not invent fields — spec keys come from the RolloutManager schema (e.g. ha, controllerResources, env, plugins, version)

evals.name: Attach a tenant namespace to a central Argo CD
evals.prompt: Our payments-dev namespace should be managed by the openshift-gitops Argo CD instance, but Applications we create there are being ignored. We already created a NamespaceManagement resource. What's wrong?
expectations: Explains that NamespaceManagement is a two-sided handshake — the tenant CR alone does nothing
Tenant side: NamespaceManagement (argoproj.io/v1beta1) in the tenant namespace with required spec.managedBy set to the Argo CD instance's namespace
Argo CD side: ArgoCD.spec.namespaceManagement entry with both name and allowManagedBy: true
Notes the failure is silent — no event or condition is raised when only one side is configured
Recommends against hand-editing --application-namespaces, which the operator resets

evals.name: Why do ArgoCD CR edits revert on the default instance
evals.prompt: Every time I patch the openshift-gitops ArgoCD CR to add infra node tolerations, the change reverts within a minute. Other ArgoCD instances on the cluster keep my edits fine.
expectations: Identifies GitopsService (pipelines.openshift.io/v1alpha1, cluster-scoped, normally named 'cluster') as the owner of the default openshift-gitops instance
Explains the ownerReference with blockOwnerDeletion on the default ArgoCD CR
Directs node placement/tolerations/imagePullPolicy for default workloads to GitopsService (runOnInfra, nodeSelector, tolerations) rather than the ArgoCD CR
Notes that a separately created ArgoCD CR in another namespace is freely editable — which is why the other instances behave differently
Suggests checking ownerReferences to confirm, e.g. kubectl get argocd openshift-gitops -n openshift-gitops -o jsonpath='{.metadata.ownerReferences}'

evals.name: Image Updater via the operator CRD
evals.prompt: Configure automated semver image updates for all Applications matching payments-* on OpenShift GitOps. The apps are Helm-based and we want the change written back to Git on the main branch.
expectations: Uses the ImageUpdater CRD with apiVersion argocd-image-updater.argocd-image-updater.argoproj.io or notes the SEPARATE API group argocd-image-updater.argoproj.io/v1alpha1 — not argoproj.io
spec.applicationRefs is present (required) with namePattern: payments-*
images[] entries use alias and imageName
Uses manifestTargets.helm (name/tag) for a Helm source, not manifestTargets.kustomize
updateStrategy: semver set via commonUpdateSettings
writeBackConfig.method: git with gitConfig.branch: main
Warns that mismatching manifestTargets to the Application source type makes the updater silently write nothing

evals.name: Resource tracking method and sync policy for a shared cluster
evals.prompt: We run Argo CD alongside Helm and a legacy deployment tool on the same cluster, and Applications keep showing resources as OutOfSync that nobody changed. What tracking and sync settings should we use?
expectations: Identifies the label-based tracking method as the likely cause — app.kubernetes.io/instance collides with other tools that set the same label
Recommends resource.trackingMethod: annotation (argocd.argoproj.io/tracking-id), which avoids the collision, and notes it is the modern default
Mentions configuring this in argocd-cm (and on OpenShift via the ArgoCD CR rather than editing the ConfigMap directly)
Recommends ignoreDifferences for fields owned by other controllers (e.g. HPA-managed replicas) rather than fighting them with selfHeal
Does not recommend disabling selfHeal as the primary fix

evals.name: Secret management choice for a GitOps repo
evals.prompt: We need database credentials available to apps deployed by Argo CD. Someone suggested just base64-encoding them into a Secret manifest in the Git repo. Advise us.
expectations: Rejects plain Secrets in Git, and states that base64 is encoding not encryption — anyone with repo read access has the credential
Presents the real options with trade-offs: Sealed Secrets, External Secrets Operator, SOPS, and Vault (via CSI or ESO)
Notes that External Secrets Operator / Vault keep the secret out of Git entirely, whereas Sealed Secrets and SOPS commit an encrypted form
Mentions that Argo CD needs to be able to decrypt or resolve whichever mechanism is chosen
Does not simply say 'use Sealed Secrets' without stating why it fits or does not fit their situation

evals.name: Choose a GitOps repository pattern
evals.prompt: We have 6 microservices going to dev, staging and prod across two clusters, and a platform team that owns cluster addons. Right now everything is one repo with a flat directory of Application manifests that we hand-edit. How should we structure this?
expectations: Compares the real options rather than asserting one — app-of-apps, ApplicationSet, monorepo, multi-repo, environment-branch — with trade-offs
Recommends ApplicationSet for the 6 services x 3 envs x 2 clusters fan-out instead of hand-maintained Application manifests, and explains that generators remove the per-combination manifest
Separates platform/cluster addons from application workloads (different ownership, different review path, often a different AppProject)
Addresses environment promotion explicitly — directory-per-env vs branch-per-env — and notes the trade-off rather than silently picking one
Warns against targetRevision: HEAD for production regardless of pattern chosen
Flags at least one anti-pattern relevant to their current layout (e.g. a flat directory of hand-edited Applications does not scale, or mixing platform and tenant resources in one AppProject)

evals.name: AppProject sync windows — allow/deny interaction and manualSync
evals.prompt: We want Argo CD to only auto-sync our production AppProject during business hours, 08:00-18:00 Monday to Friday New York time, and never during a Friday-night change freeze. On-call must still be able to sync by hand during the freeze to fix an incident. Write the AppProject syncWindows and explain how the windows combine.
expectations: Uses spec.syncWindows with kind: allow for the business-hours window and kind: deny for the change freeze
Sets timeZone (e.g. America/New_York) rather than assuming the cron schedule is in local time — schedule is UTC by default
Expresses the window as a cron schedule plus a duration, not a start/end time pair
States the combination rule correctly: with both allow and deny windows present, a sync must fall INSIDE an allow window AND OUTSIDE every deny window
Sets manualSync: true on the deny window so on-call can still sync by hand during the freeze
Explains manualSync correctly as an escape hatch that PERMITS manual syncs the window would otherwise block — not as an additional restriction, and not as something that enables automated sync
Does not claim manualSync: false adds protection beyond the window's default behaviour (false is the default and blocks manual syncs too)

evals.name: AppProject resource allow/deny lists and sourceNamespaces scoping
evals.prompt: Tenant team 'payments' should deploy only from github.com/acme/payments.git into the payments-dev and payments-prod namespaces on the in-cluster API. They must not be able to create cluster-scoped resources except Namespaces, and must not set their own ResourceQuota or LimitRange. Their Application CRs will live in the payments-dev namespace, not in openshift-gitops. Write the AppProject.
expectations: sourceRepos lists the specific repo URL, not '*'
destinations scope both namespaces to the in-cluster server (https://kubernetes.default.svc), not server: '*'
Uses clusterResourceWhitelist for the cluster-scoped allowance, listing Namespace (group "") — and does NOT use a namespace-scoped list for this
Uses namespaceResourceBlacklist for ResourceQuota and LimitRange — correctly distinguishing namespace-scoped denial from the cluster-scoped whitelist
Sets spec.sourceNamespaces to include payments-dev so Application CRs outside the Argo CD namespace are permitted by this project

Notes that sourceNamespaces on the AppProject is not sufficient on its own — the Argo CD instance must also be configured to watch that namespace (application-namespaces / .spec.sourceNamespaces on the ArgoCD CR)
Does not use a wildcard in clusterResourceWhitelist (no '*'/'*'), which would defeat the restriction

evals.name: AppProject role scoping and orphaned resource monitoring
evals.prompt: Give the payments team read-only access to their own AppProject's Applications through Argo CD RBAC, plus the ability to sync but not delete. They also want to be warned about resources left behind in their namespaces that no Application owns, without those warnings firing for ServiceAccounts and ConfigMaps that other controllers create. Configure the AppProject.
expectations: Defines spec.roles with a named role and policy lines, not cluster-level RBAC
Policy lines use the p, proj:<project>:<role>, applications, <action>, <project>/<app>, allow form — scoped to this project, not '*'
Grants get and sync actions and does NOT grant delete
Binds the role to a group via the role's groups list (OIDC/SSO group), rather than assuming a Kubernetes RoleBinding grants Argo CD UI access
Enables spec.orphanedResources with warn: true
Uses the orphanedResources ignore list to exclude ServiceAccount and ConfigMap kinds, rather than disabling orphaned-resource monitoring entirely
Does not conflate Argo CD project RBAC with Kubernetes RBAC — states that project roles govern access within Argo CD, not cluster permissions
